references.text: The immediate context: The council first asks whether Jesus is the Messiah ([ref:Luk 22:67-69|Luke 22:67-69]), and when he answers by referring to the Son of Man at God's right hand, they follow up with the question of whether he is the Son of God (v. 70).

In Matthew's parallel account, the high priest puts Jesus under oath and asks if he is "the Messiah, the Son of God", and Jesus answers "You have said so" ([ref:Matt 26:63-64|Matthew 26:63-64]) – the same type of affirmative answer as in Luke.
Mark's parallel where the high priest asks: "Are you the Messiah, the Son of the Blessed One?" and Jesus answers "I am" ([ref:Mark 14:61-62|Mark 14:61-62]).

Jesus says that the Father has set him apart and sent him into the world, and asks whether it is blasphemy to say "I am the Son of God" ([ref:Joh 10:36|John 10:36]). Here Jesus himself confirms the title "Son of God".
The Jews tell Pilate that Jesus must die because he made himself the Son of God ([ref:Joh 19:7|John 19:7]) – this shows that the claim to be the Son of God was the very charge brought against him.

Psalm 2:7 is the messianic proclamation where God says: "You are my son; today I have become your father" ([ref:Sal 2:7|Psalms 2:7]). The council's question "Are you then the Son of God?" connects to this Old Testament messianic expectation.

The demons cry out that Jesus is the Son of God, and Jesus forbids them to speak because they knew he was the Messiah ([ref:Luk 4:41|Luke 4:41]). The connection between "Son of God" and "Messiah" is the same as in the trial.
The angel Gabriel tells Mary that the child to be born will be called holy, the Son of God ([ref:Luk 1:35|Luke 1:35]). This is Luke's first introduction of the title "Son of God" for Jesus.
Jesus says "if you do not believe that I AM, you will die in your sins" ([ref:Joh 8:24|John 8:24]). The expression "ἐγώ εἰμι" in Jesus' answer in Luke 22:70 parallels this absolute "I am" statement.

Paul confesses that Jesus "was declared to be the Son of God with power by his resurrection from the dead" ([ref:Rom 1:4|Romans 1:4]). The title "Son of God" with which the council confronted Jesus was confirmed through the resurrection.
Those who mock Jesus on the cross say: "He trusts in God … for he said, I am the Son of God" ([ref:Matt 27:43|Matthew 27:43]). The charge from the trial follows him all the way to the cross.
